title: Deterministic parallel execution and safe CI sharding
criteriaSource: docs/phase-16-plan.md section 6; security criteria from the Phase 16 security program
purpose: Registered so no criterion silently loses its implementation or test.
status 'done' requires real implementation and a real test; 'partial' means implemented but the criterion's full evidence is missing (see note); 'planned' means not built or not evidenced.
tests/regression/p16-traceability.check.cjs fails on any done or partial row whose paths or tests do not exist.

verifiedByMeaning.test: An executing regression test asserts the criterion.
verifiedByMeaning.platform: Third-party platform behaviour; Falcon wiring tested, outcome evidenced on hosted runs.
verifiedByMeaning.review: Evidenced by a recorded review verdict or scan output rather than code.

criteria.title: Default and compatibility
criteria.text: Without --workers/--shard, behaviour, report shape (modulo documented additive fields) and exit codes match Phase 15; default workers is 1

tests.name: default parsing is unchanged: --workers=1 and unrelated flags are accepted by the parser
defaults
buildReport is byte-identical to the previous implementation

criteria.title: Strict flag validation
criteria.text: Invalid, duplicate, conflicting, empty, fractional, negative, zero or excessive --workers/--shard values (workers 1..16, shard total 1..64, index 1..total; bounds finalized in the architecture doc) exit non-zero before dashboard or browser start; messages are sanitized and at most 300 characters and never echo the raw value beyond 40 characters

tests.name: invalid workers values rejected
shard validation
echo is bounded and sanitized
invalid parallel flags exit 1 quickly with no browser

criteria.title: Merge command
criteria.text: A dedicated merge command exists with strict arguments and non-zero exit on any rejection

tests.name: merge command: unknown, duplicate, empty and missing args exit 2
merge command exit codes: 0 passed, 1 failed run, 2 rejected input and unexpected total
merge command

criteria.title: Canonical ordinals
criteria.text: Entry page is ordinal 0; remaining pages follow an explicitly documented total order independent of discovery timing

tests.name: canonicalOrder: entry first, code-unit sort, unique, input-order independent

criteria.title: Canonical-order dedupe
criteria.text: Deduplication runs after analysis in canonical page order; worker completion order never decides ownership, counts or trust

tests.name: dedupeInOrder: first owner keeps, same output for shuffled input
reverse completion order does not change page order or dedupe owners

criteria.title: Budget semantics
criteria.text: After the deadline no new work starts, bounded in-flight work finishes, never-started work is budget-exhausted, completed verdicts are kept, actual duration is reported, and docs do not call it a hard cap

tests.name: deadline marks remainder not-started; in-flight finishes
deadline already passed starts nothing
budget deadline marks never-started pages budget-exhausted; max-pages cut is skipped

criteria.note: Docs wording ("not a hard cap") checked by review under AC-38, not by this test.

criteria.title: Bounded scheduler
criteria.text: Active tasks never exceed --workers; queue order is deterministic; no unbounded Promise.all

tests.name: never exceeds limit active, with random delays
dispatch follows index order

criteria.title: Context isolation and cleanup
criteria.text: Every active page task uses its own browser context; contexts, pages, timers and handles are released in finally on success, failure and abort

tests.name: a failing task is isolated and every context is closed
bounded contexts, failed page row, dedupe order, bundle roundtrip, canonical state untouched

criteria.title: Auth state handling
criteria.text: With authenticated discovery, a test asserts each worker context starts with a bounded in-memory copy of storageState (size cap in the architecture doc), that no storageState file is written by default, and that a state mutation in one context is not visible in another

tests.name: bounded contexts, failed page row, dedupe order, bundle roundtrip, canonical state untouched

criteria.note: storageState is passed to newContext in ParallelSweep.js, but no test asserts the size cap, absence of a written state file, or cross-context mutation isolation as the criterion requires.

criteria.title: Partial failure salvage
criteria.text: A crashed or failed worker task keeps completed verdicts and records the failure; the run never exits 0 with missing verdicts

tests.name: throwing task is isolated and error is bounded
bounded contexts, failed page row, dedupe order, bundle roundtrip, canonical state untouched
bundle roundtrip validates and exit code reflects failures

criteria.title: Exact page coverage
criteria.text: For any frontier and N, every eligible page belongs to exactly one shard, deterministically

tests.name: shardOf partitions exactly with balanced counts for N 1..64
assignShards gives each ordinal exactly one shard
shards cover every page exactly once and bundles validate

criteria.title: Manifest
criteria.text: Each shard emits a versioned manifest with run, commit and config identity, shard index/total, assigned/completed/incomplete page identities, fragment and journal references, exit status and safe timing; the manifest is capped at a numeric size set in the architecture doc and the reader accepts the maximum and rejects maximum+1

tests.name: manifest: valid accepted
manifest: byte size max accepted, max+1 rejected
bundle roundtrip validates and exit code reflects failures

criteria.title: Merge rejection
criteria.text: Missing, duplicate, mixed-run/total/SHA/config, duplicate or missing page ownership, unknown schema, bad status/ordinal, oversized, malformed, traversal or symlink inputs are rejected: non-zero exit, no PASSED report, no canonical mutation, inputs preserved

tests.name: reject: ${name} -> code 2, canonical files unchanged, inputs kept
same event id with a different payload is rejected by the guard
expectTotal mismatch is rejected
tampered fragment, journal, manifest and analysis are rejected
invalid inputs are refused before anything is referenced

criteria.title: Byte-identical merge
criteria.text: Identical fragments merge to byte-identical output regardless of input order

tests.name: shuffled shard creation order gives byte-identical report and state

criteria.title: Sequential/parallel/sharded equivalence
criteria.text: Controlled runs are semantically identical after removing only documented volatile timestamps and durations

tests.name: p16 e2e: N=1 and N=3 merge to the same semantic report; shuffle, missing shard, crash-rerun
parallel sweep records numeric stage timings; merge carries them; volatile stripping keeps comparison stable

criteria.title: Exit codes and single report
criteria.text: Aggregate exit code reflects all shards; only the coordinator writes reports/test-report.json

tests.name: merge command exit codes: 0 passed, 1 failed run, 2 rejected input and unexpected total
shard with only passes exits 0 even with no tests run
clean merge: code 1 (a deduped+failed page), report and state written, fragments removed

criteria.note: Single-writer property (only the coordinator writes reports/test-report.json) is exercised indirectly through merge/e2e, not by a dedicated assertion.

criteria.title: Journal envelope
criteria.text: Journals and manifests are validated against a per-event-type allow-list schema with explicit numeric bounds on every field; planted canary values in every disallowed class never appear in output

tests.name: every event type: valid payload accepted
payload: missing key, unknown key, wrong type, bad enum
canaries in disallowed fields are never accepted
journal: structural tamper rejected
canaries never appear in a finished journal

criteria.title: Idempotent crash-safe merge
criteria.text: Replay, reverse order, duplicates, interruption and retry yield one canonical result; no partial success; failed inputs preserved; journals deleted only after durable persistence. Failure to persist after journals are written leaves journals in place and the run reports non-durable state with a non-zero exit

tests.name: replaying the merge is a no-op returning the recorded outcome
persist failure gives code 3, bundle files kept, no report
crash before ${step} then rerun converges to the clean-run bytes
receipt with a different input digest is rejected

criteria.title: Flakiness reducer
criteria.text: Union by stable event ID, deterministic order, no retry inflation, cap after merge

tests.name: flakiness: retry events (same id) do not inflate; also not across a different run id
flakiness: input order does not change the output
flakiness: history trimmed to newest 20 after all appends (existing items first)

criteria.title: Quarantine and healing decisions
criteria.text: Immutable attributed events; explicit decisions only; newer valid decision wins by documented rule

tests.name: flakiness: events never change quarantined; a human ledger decision wins either way
FlakinessTracker diversion surfaces bad payloads (negative path) and quarantine is never diverted
LocatorMemory decisions are never diverted

criteria.note: Healing-decision precedence is covered through the pending/locator-memory reducers; no standalone test for healing_decisions.json newer-wins.

criteria.title: Healing pending reducer
criteria.text: Earliest firstSeen, latest lastSeen, idempotent occurrences, rejection re-derived from decisions

tests.name: pending: create sets firstSeen=min, lastSeen=max, occurrences=distinct ids, tier3=1+distinct tier3 ids
pending: previouslyRejected re-derived from the fresh ledger; stale cache replaced
pending: replay twice and shuffled input are byte-identical; marker is FIFO 8

criteria.title: LocatorStore reducer
criteria.text: Deterministic alternative union, lastUsed and caps; no completion-order eviction

tests.name: locatorStore: use raises lastUsed to max only for an existing key; absent key ignored
locatorStore: alternative union preserves order, appends new, keeps newest 5, replay is a no-op
locatorStore: cap 500 evicts by (lastUsed, key); order of use events does not matter

criteria.title: LocatorMemory reducer
criteria.text: LocatorMemory merge rules are specified in the architecture doc as a decision table (human approve, human revoke, inferred, stale revision); each row has a test, and any unresolved revocation conflict yields not-approved

tests.name: row 1: absent + evidence creates trusted; firstSeen min, lastSeen max
row 8: revoked + evidence is ignored and the entry is unchanged
row 10: human decision after snapshotAt drops evidence and candidates as stale (any trust)
row 12: trusted with a revocation not older than the last approve (or unparseable/equal) fails closed

criteria.title: Healing logs
criteria.text: Private worker logs merge canonically; retries are not doubled

tests.name: healingLog: union by id in global order, HealingReport entry shape, byte-stable on replay and shuffle

criteria.title: Run history
criteria.text: Exactly one aggregate record after a successful merge, never one per shard

tests.name: clean merge: code 1 (a deduped+failed page), report and state written, fragments removed

criteria.note: Merge writes run history once, but no test asserts exactly one run_history record after merge versus one per shard.

criteria.title: Visual artifacts and logs
criteria.text: Per-worker visual diff artifacts and logs are written under worker-private directories, merged by canonical page ordinal with name-collision handling, or the feature is rejected with a documented unsupported error under --workers>1; a test exercises two workers producing the same artifact name

tests.name: VisualRegression constructor throws VISUAL_REGRESSION_UNSUPPORTED_PARALLEL and creates nothing

criteria.note: Takes the documented-unsupported branch under --workers>1; per-worker artifact merge is not built.

criteria.title: Path and identity safety
criteria.text: Run/shard/worker identifiers match a fixed pattern and length cap, are never used raw in paths, and every path built from them resolves under a trusted root with symlink refusal and restrictive permissions; tests cover traversal, absolute paths, symlinks and over-length values

tests.name: resolveUnder accepts a 64-char name and rejects 65
resolveUnder rejects traversal, absolute, NUL, separators, dots, unicode, empty
resolveUnder refuses a symlinked intermediate that escapes the root
writeAtomicPrivate: creates 0600 file in 0700 dirs, replaces atomically
run-id pattern and requirement

criteria.title: Parser and resource bounds
criteria.text: Journal, manifest and fragment size, count, nesting, array, string and event-count limits are numeric constants enforced by the reader; schemas reject __proto__/prototype/constructor and non-finite values; each limit has a test that accepts the maximum and rejects maximum+1

tests.name: Limits are frozen and match the architecture table
readBoundedJson: accepts maxBytes, rejects maxBytes+1
readBoundedJson: depth max accepted, max+1 rejected; 10k nesting rejected
readBoundedJson: forbidden keys at any depth rejected, no pollution
readBoundedJson: huge exponent (Infinity) rejected
journal: event-count cap max accepted, max+1 rejected
journal: byte cap accepts max (2 MiB), rejects max+1
manifest: pages array max accepted, max+1 rejected
fragment: byte cap accepts max and rejects max+1

criteria.title: No privilege from workers
criteria.text: Workers and mergers cannot approve healing; duplicate events cannot raise trust; branch state cannot authorize another branch

tests.name: event types: unknown and decision types rejected
record rejects unknown, decision, and task.end types
locatorStore: non-use event types (e.g. locatorStore.add from a worker) never change the store
never raises trust of an existing entry; human decision in canonical beats worker events
HealingTrust.recordPending / recordTier3Invocation divert; approve/reject never do

criteria.title: Secret canaries
criteria.text: Planted canaries never appear in journals, manifests, reports, logs or artifacts

tests.name: canaries never appear in a finished journal
record never leaks rejected content in the error
canaries in disallowed fields are never accepted
fragment: valid accepted; unknown keys and secrets in fields rejected

criteria.note: Canary coverage of journals and schemas; report/log/artifact outputs of a full run are not canary-swept end to end.

criteria.title: Accurate parallel status

tests.name: P16-AC-31: seq is strictly increasing across mixed events and survives the replay cap
P16-AC-31: broadcast and replayed events carry the same seq, still increasing after reconnect
P16-AC-31: /emit accepts valid runPlan and workerState with seq in /events
P16-AC-31: malformed runPlan/workerState are rejected with 400 and no echo

criteria.title: Security preserved

tests.name: P16-AC-32: panel shows mode, workers, shard and counts at defined points and after replay
P16-AC-32: panel renders hostile values as inert text
P16-AC-32: interleaved concurrent page events fold to correct counts (client and server)

tests.name: benchmark stats helpers
